newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power rises on fire, outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power rises on fire, outages.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. rose Wednesday on news of a substation fire in New York and continued outage of several nuclear power plants in the region.
High costs of residual fuel oil and natural gas also underpinned the recent strength in the Northeast physical market, industry sources said.

The early Wednesday fire at the Sprain Brook substation, operated by Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, in the city of Yonkers shut up to six high-voltage transmission lines, reducing the power flow from northern to southern New York. "It cut a lot of schedules," a Houston trader noted.
ConEd was heard needing to turn more expensive oil and natgas-fired generation to compensate for reduced supply from northern New York.
Moreover, nearby utilities connected to ConEd's system were sending power to assist ConEd due to restricted power flow.

In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday was assessed near $24.00-$24.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Tuesday's $24.00 quote for Wednesday delivery.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Tuesday was still valued at $14.00-$15.00.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday delivery was pegged near $34.00, sharply higher than Tuesday's range of $29.00-$30.00.
Eastern NYPP includes Long Island, New York City and Westchester County, the areas which experienced a power dip, which ConEd blamed on the Sprain Brook substation fire.
Off-peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday in eastern NYPP rose the $17.00 mark, up from Tuesday's $14.00-$15.00.

Prices in New York could ease with the return of the 1,137 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point nuclear unit 2 from its refueling outage that began on September 28. The Scriba, N.Y., station could resume service as early as Friday.
Up in the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), spot prices were pressured higher today, primarily on the ongoing shutdown of the 510 MW Vermont Yankee nuclear plant.
"Vermont Yankee seems to be a big question mark," said a Northeast marketer. The outage of the Vernon, Vt., station has been protracted by about a week.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday at the Northeast Utilities border was discussed at $36.00-$37.00, up from Tuesday's $34.00-$36.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Thursday delivery to the NU border was quoted at $20.00-$23.00, up from a quote of $19.00-$21.00 on Tuesday.
